    Validate a set of bibliographic references via OpenAlex

    validate_references.Rd

    Complete pipeline for validating a set of bibliographic references (for example extracted by Grobid) against OpenAlex. For each reference, the function first attempts validation by DOI (batched queries to OpenAlex then, if necessary, to doi.org), then completes or replaces this result with a title search when the DOI is missing, invalid, not found or inconsistent with the returned metadata. Each input reference can result in one or more output rows, one row per retained OpenAlex candidate.

    Usage

    validate_references(
  refs,
  verbose = TRUE,
  max_candidates = .checkrefr_env$oa_max_candidates
)

    Arguments

    refs

    data.frame or tibble. Bibliographic references to validate. Must contain the columns title, authors_list, doi, year, ref_n and source_file (structure typically produced by parse_references, parse_citation_list, or by process_citation_file, grobid_process_file, with the "processReferences" service and by grobid_process_files, for each, with the output_format = "parsed" parameter).

    verbose

    logical. If TRUE (default), displays the processing progress (DOI and title steps) as well as a final summary of the matching statuses obtained.

    max_candidates

    integer. Maximum number of OpenAlex candidates presented per reference. Default value: .checkrefr_env$oa_max_candidates, (initialized to 3).

    Value

    A data.frame/tibble containing one or more rows per input reference (one row per retained OpenAlex candidate, or a single row match_status = "no_match" if no candidate was found). Main columns: source_file, ref_n, input_title, input_doi, input_year, input_authors, oa_id, oa_title, oa_doi, oa_year, oa_authors, score_title, score_authors, score_year, score_global, n_candidates and match_status. Use deduplicate_references to keep only the best candidate per reference.

    Details

    Processing takes place in two main steps:

    Step 1 — Batch DOI validation: syntactically valid DOIs are extracted and queried in one or several batched requests to OpenAlex. Valid DOIs but absent from OpenAlex are then queried individually against doi.org (CSL-JSON metadata or, failing that, APA bibliographic text). Each reference then receives a status among: confirmed_with_doi, partial_with_doi, doi_mismatch, doi_not_found, doi_does_not_exist, doi_unreachable, doi_no_metadata, or no result if the reference does not have a syntactically valid DOI.

    Step 2 — Title validation, applied reference by reference according to the result of step 1:

    • If the DOI is confirmed_with_doi: only the candidates derived from the DOI are kept.

    • If the DOI is partial_with_doi, doi_mismatch, doi_not_found or doi_does_not_exist: the candidates derived from the DOI are combined with those obtained via a complementary title search.

    • If no DOI result is available (no valid DOI): only the title search is performed.

    Matching score computation: for each retained OpenAlex candidate, an overall matching score (score_global) is computed as a weighted combination of three components:

    • a title similarity score (normalized Damerau-Levenshtein distance);

    • an author similarity score, computed by compute_author_score (which itself relies on sim_author_pair for comparing each pair of names) — see the documentation of these two functions for details on the computation rules and associated parameters;

    • a publication year matching score (exact, tolerance of one year, or zero beyond that).

    The weights of this combination as well as the candidate acceptance thresholds can be configured via checkrefr_set_defaults and can be viewed via oa_matching_info. Only candidates whose overall score exceeds the configured minimum threshold are retained, up to a limit of max_candidates candidates per reference.

    See also

    compute_author_score and sim_author_pair for details on the computation of the author similarity score; oa_matching_info to view the thresholds and weights used in the computation of the overall score; deduplicate_references to keep only one candidate per reference; parse_references and parse_citation_list to produce the refs object expected as input.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# refs must contain at least: title, authors_list, doi, year, ref_n, source_file
refs <- parse_references("my_file.tei.xml")
results <- validate_references(refs, verbose = TRUE)

# Keep only the best candidate per reference
dedup_results <- deduplicate_references(results)
} # }
